title: Music Now! Musica Nostra! Forum in Mafra put music and listening at the heart of Europe’s living cultural heritage
content:
Bringing together European heritage professionals, musicians, researchers, policymakers and young people, the ‘Music Now! Musica Nostra!’ Forum took place on 7-8 November 2026 at the Royal Building of Mafra, Portugal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Through two days of discussions, musical experiences and exchanges, participants explored how music and listening can strengthen democracy, foster intercultural dialogue, safeguard living heritage and contribute to a more sustainable and peaceful Europe.

Organised by the Centre Européen de Musique, a partner of the European Heritage Hub, in collaboration with Europa Nostra, the Municipality of Mafra and the Centro Nacional de Cultura, which operates the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Lisbon, the conference built on the first ‘Music Now! Musica Nostra!’ gathering held in April 2025 and the European Manifesto it inspired. The event brought together voices from across Europe and beyond, with a particular emphasis on the role of younger generations in shaping the future of Europe’s cultural heritage.

title: Preserving memory through intergenerational collaboration in Lisbon
content:
Lisbon welcomed 19 participants during a European Heritage Hub Peer-Learning Visit from 4-6 November, exploring how community memories, oral histories and cultural heritage initiatives can strengthen social cohesion, foster intergenerational exchange and reinforce people’s sense of belonging.

Hosted by the City of Lisbon and organised in collaboration with Hub partner Eurocities, the visit focused on the municipal Memories of Lisbon Programme (Programa Memórias de Lisboa), selected as one of the Hub’s 10 Local Good Practices. The programme was led by Memory and Intangible Cultural Heritage Unit representatives Alexandra Aníbal and Mafalda Seoane.

The Memories of Lisbon Programme initiative connects a local older generation of storytellers with young people who interview, film and edit their testimonies about life in Lisbon — demonstrating how personal stories and local heritage can become powerful tools for community engagement, inclusion and cultural participation.
